question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=\ln u,\,u=3 x + 4.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=\frac{1}{u}\cdot (3) \\ &=\frac{1}{3 x + 4}\cdot (3) \\ &=\frac{3}{3 x + 4}.\end{aligned}
$$
